item.title: 307510 : I-275 East between MM 73.5 and 73.1 Area of Combs-Hehl Bridge in Campbell County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of a routine bridge inspection scheduled for the Combs-Hehl Bridge (mile point 73.1 to 73.3), which carries Interstate 275 over the Ohio River between Kentucky and Ohio. The inspection is scheduled for Monday, Oct. 5 through Friday, Oct. 16, with daytime single lane closures in place during inspection hours. Monday, Oct. 5 through Friday, Oct. 9: Crews will inspect the eastbound portion of the bridge. Single lane closures will be in place from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. daily. The lane closure will not affect access to Exit 72 (Kellogg Avenue) on the Ohio side of the bridge. Monday, Oct. 12 through Friday, Oct. 16: Crews will inspect the westbound portion of the bridge. Single lane closures will be in place from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. daily. Motorists should use caution when traveling across the bridge during inspection hours and be aware of personnel and equipment within the work zone. Drivers are encouraged to leave early, plan ahead and drive safely. Weather permitting, the inspection is expected to be completed by 2 p.m. Friday, Oct. 16. KYTC will advise if the project schedule is adjusted due to weather or other unforeseen circumstances.

item.title: 307725 : I-275 East between MM 78.5 and 77.0 Between Pride Parkway and Licking Pike in Campbell County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of a bridge maintenance project on Interstate 275 in Campbell County beginning Tuesday, Oct. 6. This project will focus on repairing potholes on the bridge deck to improve safety. On Tuesday, Oct. 6 and Wednesday, Oct. 7, crews will conduct the maintenance project on the I-275 eastbound bridge over the Licking River (78 mile point). Beginning nightly at 7 p.m., crews will block the left lane of I-275 from east of Pride Parkway (KY 16) to past the Wilder exit (KY 9). At 9 p.m., this will shift to a double lane closure (left and center lanes). All lanes will reopen by 5 a.m. daily. The exit on/off ramps to the AA Highway/KY 9 will remain open during these operations. Motorists are encouraged to find alternate routes. This work is being performed overnight to mitigate travel delays. Weather permitting, this maintenance project is expected to be completed Thursday, Oct. 8 at 5 a.m. KYTC will provide updates if additional nights of work are needed to complete the project.

item.title: 304129 : I-71 North between MM 52.7 and 57.3 Between KY-227 and KY-1039 in Gallatin County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : A widening project aimed at reducing congestion and improving safety on I-71 in Carroll and Gallatin counties is in progress. The project will widen I-71 from its configuration of two lanes in each direction, to three lanes. (Oct. 2, 2026) – The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of an upcoming traffic shift on Interstate 71 northbound as part of the ongoing widening project in Gallatin and Carroll counties. Beginning at 8 p.m. Tuesday, Oct. 6, crews will begin work to shift I-71 northbound traffic into a new configuration within the project limits. Weather permitting, the traffic shift and associated lane and ramp closures are expected to be completed by 8 a.m. Wednesday, Oct. 7. The right lane of I-71 northbound will initially be closed while crews pave and restripe the roadway in preparation for the new traffic pattern. Several northbound on/off ramps will also be blocked during the first portion of the overnight work. Impacted ramps include: I-71 northbound off-ramp to Exit 55 (KY 1039) I-71 northbound off-ramp to Exit 57 (KY 35/Sparta Pike) Exit 57 (KY 35/Sparta Pike) on-ramp to I-71 northbound Various lane closures will continue throughout the night as crews prepare the roadway for the shift. Once preparations are complete, crews will use a rolling roadblock to safely place barrels and transition northbound traffic into the new configuration. Motorists should expect temporary delays while the rolling roadblock is in progress. Once the traffic shift is complete, two lanes of I-71 northbound will reopen, along with access to northbound entrance and exit ramps. Motorists should use caution while traveling through the area, expect changing traffic conditions and pay close attention to the new lane configuration, signage and traffic control devices. The speed limit in the work zone has been reduced to 55 MPH, and law enforcement will be on-site to ensure compliance. Please, drive carefully throughout the work zone. Weather permitting, the overall project is expected to be completed Nov. 1, 2026. Learn more about the project at https://driving-nky-progress-kytc.hub.arcgis.com/pages/i-71-widening-gallatincarroll-counties.

item.title: 269220 : I-71 North-South between MM 0.1 and 2.0 Between I-64/I-71 Interchange and Zorn Ave. in Jefferson County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : The I-71 widening and improvement project is a $50 million infrastructure investment to enhance safety and improve mobility along one of Louisville's most critical travel corridors. The two-year project, focused on increasing traffic capacity and safety, will enhance regional connectivity, provide reliable travel for years to come, and support economic growth. The project spans approximately two miles of interstate from the I-65/I-71 interchange near Frankfort Avenue to the I-71/Zorn Avenue interchange. Additional improvements include the construction of a multi-use path along Zorn Avenue between the I-71/Zorn Avenue interchange and Mellwood Avenue, as well as a new median treatment at the intersection of Zorn Avenue and Mellwood Avenue to enhance safety and better define traffic movements. The project also includes the demolition and reconstruction of the I-71 bridge over Beargrass Creek, along with a latex overlay on the I-71 bridge over I-64 at mile point 0.3 to extend the structure’s service life. For additional information, please visit https://transportation.ky.gov/DistrictFive/Pages/I-71-Widening---Louisville-.aspx.

item.title: 292980 : I-71/75 North Ramp to 12th Street/MLK Jr. Boulevard in Kenton County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : (June 5, 2026) – Interstate 71/75 ramp closures and detours in Covington are needed to safely advance construction on the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor Project, which will add interstate lanes, better access, a new companion bridge and convert the existing bridge for local travel to improve safety and increase regional highway capacity. Temporary closures and detours will now begin on Monday, June 8, and will take place in multiple phases. On Monday, June 8, the following closures are expected to take place: I-71/75 northbound off-ramp to 12th Street/MLK Jr. Blvd. (0.0 - 0.28 mile points): this closure will remain in place through Summer 2027. Detour: Traffic will use the I-71/75 northbound 5th Street exit ramp, turn left (north) onto Philadelphia Street, then left onto 4th Street driving west to the I-71/75 southbound ramp to Pike Street. Turn left on to Pike Street, then right on to Simon Kenton Way, then left on to MLK Blvd. KYTC will provide further updates ahead of the closures to inform all road users via the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor project website. item.title: 303284 : I-71 North between MM 56.6 and 59.9 Between Sparta Pike and Boone Road in Gallatin County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : A road rehabilitation project between Sparta Pike (KY 35) and northeast of the Boone Road (KY 465) overpass is in progress. Crews are performing pavement rehab, shoulder repairs and some guardrail work on various sections in the project area. On Friday, Sept. 25, crews will close Exit 57 (KY 35/Sparta Pike) on-ramp to I-71 northbound from 7 p.m. to 4:30 a.m. to perform paving operations on the ramp. Motorists should expect single lane closures during daytime hours, and double lane closures in the project area during evening/overnight hours. This project will occur in multiple phases, each with their own set of travel changes and lane closures. KYTC will advise ahead of any of these changes. ​ Learn more about the project here [links-1.govdelivery.com]. Weather permitting, this project is expected to be completed Nov. 15, 2026.

item.title: 303512 : I-64 West between MM 35.0 and 32.0 Between KY 55/Taylorsville Road in Shelby County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of daily blasting operations on Interstate 64 West beginning Wednesday, Sept. 2. Blasting operations are expected to occur on weekdays at approximately 2 p.m. on I-64 West between mile markers 32 and 35 (between KY 55/Taylorsville Road and KY 53/Mt Eden Road). Intermittent roadblocks are required during blasting, and delays of up to 20 minutes are possible between 1 p.m. and 3 p.m. daily. Motorists should use caution, follow posted signage, and allow extra travel time during the roadblocks. Blasting operations may be canceled on short notice due to weather or unforeseen circumstances. The interstate project is expected to be completed by the Fall of 2027.

item.title: 304488 : I-471 North-South between MM 3.7 and 5.0 Area of Daniel Carter Beard Bridge in Campbell County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : UPDATE (Thursday, Sept. 10): due to inclement weather, the traffic switch scheduled for yesterday, Wednesday, Sept. 9, has been postponed to tonight (Thursday, Sept. 10). Weather permitting, beginning at 8 p.m., motorists should expect various lane closures on Interstate 471 southbound from south of the Dave Cowens Drive (KY 8X) exit (Exit 5) to south of Memorial Parkway (3.7 mile point), a distance of 1.3 miles. Once completed, traffic will shift to the right toward the outside wall. Access to the Memorial Parkway on/off ramps to and from I-471 will be maintained during the traffic switch. On Friday, Sept. 11, crews will install temporary barrier wall to provide a safe area for repairs to be made to the median wall. This work will require various northbound and southbound lane closures beginning at 8 p.m. All lanes are expected to reopen by 6 a.m. on Saturday, Sept. 12. Once this is completed, work will begin on a containment system underneath the bridge overpass. Various evening/overnight lane closures should be expected as the project progresses. Three lanes of I-471 southbound and northbound will be maintained during daytime hours to mitigate travel delays. Euro Paint LLC is contracted to perform the $1,758,697 project on behalf of KYTC. Weather permitting, the overall project has an expected completion date of Nov. 15, 2026.

item.title: 306792 : I-71/75 North-South Between Kyles Lane and KY/OH Border in Kenton County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of nightly lane closures on Interstates 71/75 in Kenton County beginning Monday, Sept. 28. Crews will be performing electrical work as part of the ongoing Brent Spence Bridge Corridor project. This work will require a nightly northbound and southbound left lane closure from Kyles Lane (KY 1072) (188.52 mile point) to the Brent Spence Bridge (191.63 mile point), a distance of 3.11 miles. Both left lanes (northbound and southbound) will be blocked from 8 p.m. to 5 a.m. All lanes will reopen by 5 a.m. No lane closures associated with this portion of the project will be in place from Thursday, Oct. 8 through Sunday, Oct. 11 due to BLINK. Weather permitting, this portion of the project is expected to be completed Friday, Oct. 23. Project schedules are subject to change due to inclement weather or other unforeseen circumstances.

item.title: 254857 : I-264 East-West between MM 21.5 and 22.9 Area of US-42 in Jefferson County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : UPDATE (March 23, 2026) – The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of overnight lane and ramp closures on Interstate 264 East and West (Watterson Expressway) beginning Tuesday, March 24, as part of the $130 million widening and improvement project of I-264 and U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) [links-1.govdelivery.com]. Beginning Tuesday, March 24, at 8 p.m., through Wednesday, March 25, at 6 a.m.: Alternating lane closures will occur on I-264 East and West between mile markers 23 and 22 (from the I-264/I-71 split to U.S. 42/Brownsboro Road). Beginning Wednesday, March 25, at 8 p.m., through Thursday, March 26, at 6 a.m.: The I-264 East ramp to I-71 South will be closed. Motorists should continue on I-264 East, take I-71 North, then follow I-265 North to reconnect with I-71 South. Alternating lane closures will occur on I-264 East between mile markers 23 and 22 (from the I-264/I-71 split to U.S. 42/Brownsboro Road). Motorists should heed signage, use caution when traveling through the work zone, and plan ahead for travel delays. The highway improvement project is expected to be completed by the Fall of 2027. More details, including project timelines and traffic impacts [links-1.govdelivery.com], will be shared online as work progresses. Motorists are encouraged to sign up for email or text alerts [links-1.govdelivery.com] regarding weekly traffic impacts pertaining to the project.
